data.title: In Memory of the Old Kalumbatan Mosque : The Node of Reconnection : Defragmenting the Living Space.
data.description:
Team in Charges :
Yuan Viero Mahendra
Ahmad Ubaydillah
David Irzha Risqon
Roufiq Rayjendra

Status :
Second Places Winner
More than merely a physical entity above the waters, this landscape captures a moment of spatial catharsis. The Memoriam Mosque stands as a node, mediating the history of fragmentation caused by the earthquake and tsunami in 2000. Its circular mass symbolizes the endless unity and harmony between humanity and the marine environment. Supported by an adaptive floating deck system, this structure does not seek to conquer nature or erase the ruins of the past. Instead, it chooses to anchor beside them, breathing in rhythm with the tides, standing as a witness that the identity of the Children of the Sea will never be submerged by time.

My deepest gratitude to the Bajo Tribe (The Children of the Sea) in Banggai. Your resilience, history, and profound spiritual bond with the ocean have been the soul and greatest inspiration behind this creation. This is a tribute to your enduring identity.

data.title: Badaan Park Magelang City : Pusparagam in Initiation (DEI)
data.description:
Pusparagam symbolizes the beauty and
diversity woven into a single, harmonious
spatial whole—a city park
designed with a commitment to always
upholding the principles of Diversity, Equality,
and Inclusion. The creation of a space that is not merely
a city park, but also a form of
spatial initiative for a dynamic
community, thereby fostering
a sense of shared ownership and connection
among one another. A city park designed
as an initiative to embrace the diversity
of community groups and their respective
activities—spanning all age groups,
racial groups, and ethnic groups—so that all
segments of society can
experience a sense of equality despite the
real differences among the groups around us.

data.title: Reciprocal Vibrancy : Ripples of Connected Places and Shared Opportunities
data.description:
Does an area always need to have a single center to come alive?

We view cities differently. A place isn’t always just a center that influences its surroundings. It can be both a center and a supporter of other places, giving and receiving from one another, and bringing them to life.

In the context of Creative Zone: Riverfront by JXB, this idea reimagines the relationship between BNI City Station, Karet Station, Riverfront, the Dukuh Atas TOD, and the surrounding communities.

“Reciprocal Vibrancy” serves as the overarching concept for building these connections: when one place brings vitality to another, and at the same time receives that vitality in return.

From there emerges “Ripples”—ripples that begin at a single point, then spread out, meet other ripples, and create a broader impact.

It’s not merely about connecting spaces, but transforming spaces into places; bringing forth activities, interactions, identities, and opportunities that can grow together.

Because ultimately, a city doesn’t thrive because of a single center.
A city thrives when every place is able to invigorate one another.

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

data.title: PIAR House
data.description:
PiaR House reinterprets American Classic architecture through balanced symmetry, refined architectural detailing, and carefully composed spatial relationships. Natural stone, elegant moldings, and layered shadows create visual depth while maintaining clarity and restraint. Inside, generous volumes are shaped by natural daylight. A central void connects the living spaces vertically, while the courtyard strengthens the dialogue between architecture and landscape.
Rather than expressing luxury through excess, the design celebrates refinement through proportion, atmosphere, and thoughtful detailing.

data.title: WH Coffe Shop
data.description: Based in Yogyakarta, WH Coffee Shop wanted its interior to double as a brand statement. Rather than treating decor as an afterthought, we designed a full-height backlit shelving wall to display a rotating collection of ceramic and sculptural pieces, turning what's usually a plain service counter into the visual anchor of the room. Paired with a blue-and-white tile palette that runs through the entire space, the interior does the work a logo alone can't, it makes the brand legible in three dimensions.
